      "id": "https://docs.hypertask.ai/changelog/2026-11-09-group-table-rows-by-tag-htpr-8630/",
      "title": "Group table rows by tag",
      "content_text": "Table view used to group rows by board column only. Seeing the whole backlog by topic meant keeping one saved view per tag.\n\nNow table view has a **Group** control with two choices, **Column** and **Tag**. Tag mode shows one foldable group per label, with the number of tickets in its header. A ticket with two tags appears under both. Tickets with no tag sit in a **No tag** group at the end. Filters still apply, so a Status Backlog filter plus Group by Tag shows the backlog split by topic.\n\nThe choice saves with the view, so it comes back the way you left it.\n\n## Related tickets\n\n- [HTPR-8630](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/8630)",
      "summary": "Table view can group rows by tag instead of only by column, so one screen can show the backlog split by topic.",

      "id": "https://docs.hypertask.ai/changelog/2026-10-31-agents-follow-star-remind-htpr-8217/",
      "title": "Agents follow, star and set a reminder on a ticket",
      "content_text": "An agent could not keep track of a ticket the way a person does. It can now:\n\n- Follow a ticket, so it appears in that ticket's follower list until the agent unfollows.\n- Star a ticket, which bookmarks it privately for that agent. Unstar removes it.\n- Set a reminder on a ticket. The ticket comes back to the agent's inbox at that time, and a later reminder replaces an earlier one that has not fired.\n- Read all three states back in one call.\n\nThe same tool is available in AI chat. Board access, the agent write role and a ticket switch still apply, and a person's own app writes are unchanged.\n\nRelated ticket [https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/8217](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/8217).\n\n## Related tickets\n\n- [https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/8217](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/8217)",
      "summary": "An agent can now follow a ticket, star it and set a reminder on it, the same way a person can, and read its own state back.",
      "tags": [
        "Agents",
        "Tickets"
      ],
      "date_published": "2026-10-31T00:00:00.000Z",

      "id": "https://docs.hypertask.ai/changelog/2026-10-31-agents-share-a-ticket-htpr-8216/",
      "title": "Agents share a ticket and read its public link",
      "content_text": "An agent could not share a ticket. A person shares one with a button; an agent had to wait for someone to copy the link. An agent can now:\n\n- Make a ticket public on a board that allows sharing, and get the public link back, ready to hand to a client.\n- Read back whether the ticket is public, and which link is live, so a client link is never stale or invented.\n- Ask for the same ticket twice and get the same live link back instead of a second one.\n\nA ticket shared by one person counts as public for everyone who can already read it. A deleted ticket, an archived board and a ticket the agent cannot reach answer with a plain refusal. Board access, the agent write role and a ticket switch still apply, and a person's own Share button is unchanged.\n\nRelated ticket [https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/8216](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/8216).\n\n## Related tickets\n\n- [https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/8216](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/8216)",

      "id": "https://docs.hypertask.ai/changelog/2026-10-30-agents-ask-their-owner-for-board-access-htpr-7582/",
      "title": "Agents ask their owner for board access, approved in one click",
      "content_text": "An agent that needs a board it cannot reach no longer stalls with a refusal only. It can ask:\n\n- The agent sends an access request with the board and a short reason.\n- The owner gets it in Inbox Decisions and approves or declines in one click.\n- Approving adds the agent as a plain member of that board, the same as ticking Board access by hand. No role changes.\n- Declining adds nothing and tells the agent.\n- A request expires after seven days.\n\nOnly the agent's owner can decide, and only for a board in the same team. The agent can read its own request to see the state and the next step.\n\nRelated ticket [https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7582](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7582).\n\n## Related tickets\n\n- [https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7582](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7582)",
      "summary": "An agent that is not on a board can ask its owner for access. The owner approves or declines in Inbox Decisions, and approving adds the agent as a plain member.",
      "tags": [
        "Agents",
        "Boards"

      "date_published": "2026-10-30T00:00:00.000Z",

    {
      "id": "https://docs.hypertask.ai/changelog/2026-10-29-ai-chat-changes-your-settings-with-apply-and-undo-htpr-7622/",
      "title": "AI chat changes your settings, with Apply and Undo",
      "content_text": "On any Settings page, the AI chat now knows which settings are on that page. Ask for a change in plain words, such as \"switch me to the dark theme\" or \"make Anna an admin on this board\", and it answers with one card that shows the setting, the current value and the new value. Nothing changes until you press **Apply**; press **Cancel** and nothing happens. After a change lands, the card offers **Undo**, which puts the previous value back.\n\nThe AI can only do what you could do by clicking. It uses your own rights, so a board member cannot change what only the board owner may change, and every people or access change needs the same confirmation card. If a change is not something it can make, it says where the setting lives and opens that page for you.\n\nThis release is on for the owner and QA first.     {
      "id": "https://docs.hypertask.ai/changelog/2026-10-21-login-guided-start-htpr-7519/",
      "title": "A guided start after agent login",
      "content_text": "Run `hypertask login --token <token> --human` to see your signed-in identity, the newest board across all boards your token can see, and three commands to try next for write agents. A missing board title falls back to the short name. Read-only agents get two steps, list and playbook, with no create step. For example, Claude Code working for Maria Lopez could start on Product Launch, board 9142.\n\nJSON output keeps `success`, `saved`, and `configPath`. It adds `signedInAs`, `board`, and `nextSteps`. If you can see several boards, a `moreBoards` hint points to `hypertask project list`.\n\nWith no board, `--human` says \"No board yet. Create one in your Hypertask web app.\" The CLI waits at most about 1.5 seconds for the guide. On timeout, network or server error, login still saves the token and returns the previous output.\n\nMCP hello and the hello API now include `agent`, `startBoard`, and `nextSteps`: three for write agents, two for read-only agents, or none without a board. The CLI prints the server's steps. Each step has a CLI command and an MCP tool call matching the same credential's `tools/list` catalog.\n\nMCP v2 (consolidated tools, on for Everyone) uses `hypertask_tasks` with `action: \"list\"` or `\"create\"`, and `hypertask_projects` with `action: \"playbook\"`, with board and task fields under `input`.       "title": "MCP: Don't create false error when missing PR link",
      "content_text": "Before, linking to a non-existent repository sent an error and filed a ticket automatically. After, Hypertask logs a warning when the target repository is not reachable; the original task description includes that warning without automatically creating an error ticket.\n\nPrivate GitHub repositories are often unavailable to agents. This change prevents cluttered boards with errors for legitimate absent remotes, letting agents handle missing PRs manually or raise appropriate follow-up tasks instead.\n\nHow it works:\n- When an MCP tool attempts to resolve a PR URL and the repository cannot be found, Hypertask returns an error that the task creator can choose to ignore or treat as actionable.\n- A warning is recorded on the task; no automatic ticket creation occurs.\n- Agents that rely on PR linking can adjust their workflows to gracefully handle missing remotes (e.g., create a follow-up task to verify the repository visibility or use a different integration).\n\nRelated tickets: [HTPR-7279](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7279)\n\n## Related tickets\n\n- [https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7279](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7279)",

      "id": "https://docs.hypertask.ai/changelog/2026-10-14-ai-writes-use-text-compression-for-turbopuffer-upserts-htpr-7212/",
      "title": "AI writes use text compression for Turbopuffer upserts",
      "content_text": "AI-generated write to search is built on Turbopuffer embeddings for comments and pages. The underlying embed service can refuse very long or empty text. This change has the embed service reject long/empty text and rotate to a compressed representation before attempting an upsert. During upserts the embed service can still reject, at which point the write silently skips final vector generation, stores compact representation for reprocessing, and upserts without vectors. As a result:\n\n- AI-questions and AI drafts in comments and pages are now searchable with their original tags even when vectors aren’t generated (HTPR-7212).\n- Past comment embeddings that failed long/empty rejections are reprocessed, improving retrieval (HTPR-7212).\n- Updates to affected page and comment content use the compressed path, avoiding rejections (HTPR-7213, HTPR-7215, HTPR-7216).\n\nThis aligns with behavior on Vercel: page upsert and comment upsert skipped when the embed service refused, per https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7212.\n\n## Related tickets\n\n- [https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7212](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7212)",
      "summary": "AI-generated content for comments and pages is now compressed before upserting, silently rotating text when the embedding service refuses it so content remains searchable with proper tags (HTPR-7212, HTPR-7213, HTPR-7215, HTPR-7216).",
      "tags": [
        "AI",

      "content_text": "Old-style AI tool connections use Server-Sent Events (/sse) through the MCP server. Previously, a quiet connection would drop after a short idle period. After this fix, the server sends a small keep-alive heartbeat every 60 seconds to keep the connection alive. The connection then closes cleanly after a primary soft timeout (about 13 minutes). This improved reliability lets agents run schedules with long idle windows without losing connection.\n\nAn additional behavior is enforced through the *Hypertask Tasks* MCP tool.     {
      "id": "https://docs.hypertask.ai/changelog/2026-10-13-board-and-saved-view-access-security-fix-htpr-7166/",
      "title": "Board and saved-view access security fix",
      "content_text": "Board and saved-view endpoints now properly restrict access to boards you’re a member of. Commenters and thread responders may wish to revisit existing board-visibility references to ensure board-scoped behavior is clearly explained. ([HTPR-7166](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7166))\n\n### What’s changed\n\n- **Saved-view access gating** – Requests to saved-view endpoints now check board membership before returning or mutating data. Users not on the board see `404 Not Found` when trying to fetch, rename, delete, or switch to such views.\n- **Cross-board data leakage closed** – Column names, settings, and pages from other boards are no longer visible through CLI (`view show / board`, `--tasks`), MCP tools saved-view reads, or board/chat API calls.\n\n### How it works\n\nWhen a request specifies a saved view, the backend loads that view’s `view_query` payload and resolves which board owns it. If the signed-in session belongs to that board, endpoints proceed; otherwise they return `404 Not Found` rather than leaking partial board metadata or performing side effects. This prevents users from borrowing an invite or leveraging saved-view references to reach boards they do not share.\n\n### Why this matters\n\n- **Stronger security boundaries** – Invites and saved views can no longer indirectly expose cross-board data.\n- **Consistent with access semantics** – Saved-view behavior now matches board-readable resource behavior (tasks, tables, pages), which also enforce board-scoped access for anyone signed in.\n\n### Related tickets\n\n- [HTPR-7166](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7166) – Production verification after roll-forward on 2026-10-13.\n\n## Related tickets\n\n- [https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7166](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7166)",
      "summary": "Saved-view endpoints now reject access for users not on the owning board. Cross-board columns, pages, and settings are no longer readable through chat, MCP, or saved views.",

The fix prevents cross-board data leakage in the related-tasks display flow.\n\n- **HTPR-7155**: Read-only agents can no longer add, change, archive, or restore task pages. Page actions are now refused to read-only agents, preserving existing page state unchanged.\n\n- **HTPR-7162**: Board invites now only add the signed-in person to the board the invite was created for. Invites intended for one board are refused when attempted on a different team’s board. Join requests without login are refused.       "id": "https://docs.hypertask.ai/changelog/2026-10-13-board-column-names-and-settings-hidden-to-unauthorized-users-htpr-7172/",
      "title": "Board column names and settings hidden to unauthorized users",
      "content_text": "Hypertask now enforces strict board membership gating for reading board-level resources, ensuring users only see columns, layout settings, and configuration for boards they are members of. Previously, any signed-in user could read arbitrary column names and settings, including through search filters and tables, creating a potential data discovery issue across unrelated workspaces.\n\n**Users gain:**\n\n- Prevention of cross-board data discovery: unauthorized users cannot enumerate columns or settings on boards they are not on.\n- Properly scoped searches and tables: global search, filtered tables, and the search screen only return content accessible to the current user.\n- Consistent access semantics: page access follows the task; once a task moves to another board, its pages are restricted to the new board's membership.\n\n**How it works:**\n\nBackend validation now inspects board membership before returning column schemas, column names, layout filters, and board settings for tasks, tables, pages, and saved views. Requests representing cross-board reads receive `404 Not Found` or are filtered to empty results, mirroring the user’s effective board visibility. Write operations (CLI, MCP, REST) continue to be gated separately before mutation.\n\nThis security update applies to all surfaces including board detail answers, saved-view actions, and AI‑chat integrations that render table or column data. ([HTPR-7172](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7172))\n\n## Related tickets\n\n- [https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7172](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7172)",

      "content_text": "Fixed security issues with board page and column visibility. Users work only with tasks, pages, and columns that belong to boards they can actually see. The security tests demonstrated the issue and confirmed the fix works on the live site:\n\n* **Page access follows tasks** – moving a task to another board now moves its associated pages and closes them for users who cannot see the target board.\n* **Table and column filtering** – any logged-in user can no longer inspect column names or settings from boards they are not members of. Requests for such data now return `null/Project`\n* **Cross-board leaks eliminated** – before, a board member could open test pages or search across any board, exposing additional columns. After the fix, only the user’s own boards satisfy searches and loads; cross-board queries are blocked.\n\nThese changes only surface properly filtered content. No API surface or configuration is required, but the permission enforcement now explicitly evaluates board membership for both direct visibility and permission secrets.\n\n## Related tickets\n\n- [https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7154](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7154)",
      "summary": "Moving a task now follows its pages and tables to other boards, closing pages and columns to users who lack access. Security test showed the fix stops cross-board leaks.",

        "Board",
        "Security",
        "Pages"

      "id": "https://docs.hypertask.ai/changelog/2026-10-13-instant-signup-now-treats-gmail-aliases-as-taken-htpr-7159/",
      "title": "Instant signup now treats Gmail aliases as taken",
      "content_text": "Before this change, a stranger could copy an existing Gmail address with alternate spellings - like dots, +tags, or googlemail.com - and register a new account with the same identity. This allowed attackers to rename or take over someone else's account.\n\n**What users gained:**\n- Quick signup now treats all valid Gmail address forms as the same user - preventing strangers from creating a new identity from the same email.\n- Anyone arriving at the signup form sees immediate feedback if the email is already taken.\n\n**What changed on the server:**\n- Signup now performs a permissive email lookup using canonicalised Gmail address forms (user@gmail.com, user@gmail.com, user+@gmail.com, and user@gmail.com).\n- If any form matches an existing account, signup is blocked and the existing account is surfaced instead.\n\nThis fix closes a vector by which an attacker could claim ownership of an existing user's account via alternate Gmail spellings. (Live verification on app.hypertask.ai confirms HTPR-7159.)\n\n## Related tickets\n\n- [https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7159](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7159)",

      "content_text": "Hypertask adds stricter access control around board invites to prevent cross-team and cross-board usage.\n\nWhen you create an invite to a board:\n\n- An invite is only valid for the board it was generated on.\n- The signed-in person must be in the same context as the intended board; an invite for Board A is refused if used on Board B (even if the account has access to both).\n- An unauthenticated or anonymous request to use an invite is refused.\n\nThis change ensures that sharing via invite remains a scoped, safe mechanism for granting board-level access without exposing team boundaries.\n\nIf an invite is used outside its intended context, Hypertask returns a refusal to join, and no unauthorized board addition occurs.\n\n## Related tickets\n\n- [https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7162](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7162)",

      "title": "Ticket page no longer shifts on mobile",
      "content_text": "A Content Layout Shift (CLS) regression resurfaced after fix [HTPR-6899](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/6899), where the comment box on mobile ticket pages would position itself beneath the task description instead of immediately below the last comment. During page loads, components would settle into place after the initial paint, causing the interface to jitter.\n\nThe regression was identified when comment box content would shift down roughly 90‑220 px as comments loaded on long threads. Quick comparisons showed desktop shifts dropping from about 0.018 to 0.007, while mobile was worse.\n\nThe fix ensures comment boxes and thread content load in their final position instantly. Valentin's Live QA on 2026‑10‑11 passed 20 of 20 fresh loads on two accounts across desktop and phone; shift scores improved and visual elements now appear as part of cached data instead of settling afterward.\n\n**What users see:**\n- Comments open at the bottom of the task, exactly where they were expected to appear after [HTPR-6955](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/6955)'s repositioning fix.\n- No mid-page spacing around the comment area; the task body remains a stable container.\n- Same layout behavior on both desktop and mobile for all test accounts.\n\n## Related tickets\n\n- [https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7074](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7074)",

      "title": "Unified MCP endpoint address",
      "content_text": "The official MCP endpoint is now `mcp.hypertask.ai/mcp`, advertised consistently across documentation, the MCP settings dialog, and CLI configuration. This provides a single canonical address for users and agents to discover and connect to Hypertask's MCP server.\n\nWhen connecting from `mcp.hypertask.ai/mcp`, the server treats each request with a bearer token and ignores session IDs for a limited stateless path (available to Owner and QA users only). Other clients can continue using session-backed transport with WebSocket connections and SSE fallbacks.\n\nThe legacy app address (`app.hypertask.ai/mcp`) remains functional for authenticated, signed-in calls for backward compatibility, but new sign-ins are directed to the canonical endpoint. This establishes a clear path forward while maintaining compatibility for existing integrations.\n\nHTPR-7193: <a href=\"https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7193\">https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7193</a>\n\n## Related tickets\n\n- [https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7193](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7193)",

      "id": "https://docs.hypertask.ai/changelog/2026-10-13-validated-login-cookies-after-sign-out-htpr-7158/",
      "title": "Validated login cookies after sign-out",
      "content_text": "A copied or reused login cookie no longer grants continued access once its owner signs out. The system now properly invalidates cookies and refreshes sessions upon sign-out, preventing attackers from reusing expired credentials.\n\n**What users gained:**\n- Logout now fully invalidates login cookies in both the browser and Better Auth sessions on the server.\n- A valid sign-out prevents copied, reused, or post-sign-in shares of the original ht_session cookie from granting continued access.\n\n**What changed on the server:**\n- Sign-in handlers and legacy routes now always enforce signed ht_session cookie validation.\n- Better Auth sessions are refreshed and only associated with the current session ID, ensuring invalidating one sign-out clears all associated credentials.\n\nThis fix closes the gap where a session token persisted beyond its intended use after the user signed out. (Live verification on app.hypertask.ai confirms HTPR-7158.)\n\n## Related tickets\n\n- [https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7158](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7158)",
      "summary": "Copied login cookies no longer work after sign-out. Sessions are now invalidated on logout, closing a security gap where stale cookies kept working.",

      "content_text": "API-created tasks now appear in search within seconds after creation, without requiring a title rename or edit to trigger indexing. Previously, tickets created through the API or quick-add on a board would not appear in search until their title was saved again.\n\n**How it works:**\n\nThe POST /api/v1/tasks endpoint now initiates a search index update after each creation. On desktop and mobile, new tasks indexed via the API or quick-add are discoverable within a few seconds. Background indexing caches result payloads for publisher handles and subjects, reducing redo logic.\n\n**Detected use cases:**\n\nAPI-created tasks join search results alongside manual creation. Quick-add from boards and fullscreen new-task windows follow the same pattern. Reindexed tasks show title search results consistent with board/card structure and task-type tags.\n\n**Evidence:**\n\nLive test passed on 2026-10-11:\n- Ticket made via API found in search after ~6 seconds.\n- Quick-add from board found after ~3 seconds.\n- Fullscreen new-ticket window found after ~3 seconds.\n\nSee [https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7131](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7131)\n\n## Related tickets\n\n- [https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7131](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7131)",

      "content_text": "**Owner+QA preview:** Typed person filters for from: and assignee: now match every person whose name or email contains the text, ignoring case and accents. People picked from the list stay exact match.\n\nWhen you type a name for `from:` and `assignee:`, it matches every visible person whose name or email contains that text, ignoring case and accents. For example, `from:valentin` finds Valentin Yeo and any account named valentinyeo.\n\n- **Typed filters**: `from:valentin`, `assignee:yc`, and `-from:valentin` treat the name as a substring.\n- **Picker filters**: A person selected from the autocomplete list is matched exactly.\n- **Flag**: The behavior is behind `<flag:htpr-6881-search-fuzzy-person>` on for Owner and QA accounts only.\n\nUsing `dates:`, `label:`, `board:`, `has:`, and `is:` is unaffected.       "content_text": "A person's plain comment on a ticket now reliably notifies all assigned and following agents in their in-app inbox and through your configured webhook integrations. This change closes the gap between human and agent workflows, ensuring team members are immediately aware of updates that affect them without cluttering notifications with their own reflections.\n\nFor a comment author, the experience remains the same: type your message as you normally would on a ticket. The system no longer echoes back the author as a recipient, so your own comment won't trigger an extra notification for you.\n\nFor agents and any other interested listeners, the ticket's comment appears at the top of their inbox as a new item, sorted by recent updates. The change applies across desktop and mobile, and works with the existing webhook pipeline-if you've connected Slack, email, or another tool via webhooks, those integrations receive the notification alongside the in-app inbox.\n\nWhat changed\n- Added post-comment routing logic for inbox notification targets\n- Updated webhook payload structure to include comment author and assignment context\n- Guard against self-notification by marking comment author as excluded from recipient lists\n\nHow it affects you\n- Assigned agents and anyone following a ticket now see every human comment arrive instantly\n- You can rely on the inbox and webhooks as a single source of truth for task-related updates\n- No manual @mentions are required for this behavior to take effect; it applies to all plain comments\n\nThe inbox is already the place where team members process notifications efficiently, so this change strengthens its role as the central hub for task discussions. Webhook recipients maintain their existing integration logic while now receiving consistent, complete notification data.\n\n## Related tickets\n\n- [https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7088](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7088)",

      "id": "https://docs.hypertask.ai/changelog/2026-10-07-inbox-bulk-undo-works-correctly-htpr-6989/",
      "title": "Inbox bulk undo works correctly",
      "content_text": "Undoing inbox items now correctly handles bulk operations. Previously, pressing Ctrl+Z after archiving multiple items using Shift+E would say it worked but leave items in their archived state.\n\nThe undo path now gracefully skips empty row slots in the data structure instead of blocking. QAs verified the fix on both QA and normal accounts: archived 3 items at once, pressed Ctrl+Z, and all 3 items came back and stayed after reloading. Undoing a single item still works as expected.\n\nThe fix applies to bulk undo via snack bar buttons on desktop and the row's action menu. If an undo doesn't restore an item as expected, it may be located in a separate cluster or split excluded from the undo scope.\n\nRelated changes prevent crashes by ensuring the inbox list stays stable when undoing items with irregular row data ([HTPR-6527](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/6527)).\n\n## Related tickets\n\n- [https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/6989](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/6989)",

      "content_text": "Claude Haiku 5.5 has been released as the new default AI model for everyone, replacing Haiku 4.5. The change brings consistent model behavior across all AI surfaces including AI Task Writer, Agent Chat, and code-generation workflows.\n\n**Model choice and behavior:**\n- Haiku 5.5 now serves as the default model for all new AI conversations\n- The replacement reduces confusion around having multiple Haiku versions live simultaneously\n- Model quality reflects real-world usage patterns and usage-based cost\n\n**Real-world cost:**\nIn live measurements on the QA Sandbox board, Claude Haiku 5.5 costs approximately 1.7x more per request than GPT 6 Luna. This difference stems from longer answer lengths rather than per-token pricing parity:\n\n```\nAI chat, 10 prompts each on the same board:\n- Haiku 5.5: 1.70x cost of GPT 6 Luna per request\n- All models use identical per-token pricing\n```\n\nThe model is fully operational on all supported environments including Free and paid subscription tiers.\n\nWhen Haiku 5.5 is selected (or left as default), it behaves equivalently to GPT 6 Luna in all supported AI workflows, ensuring predictable outputs regardless of model provider.\n\n[https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7010](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7010)\n\n## Related tickets\n\n- [https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7010](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/7010)",

      "id": "https://docs.hypertask.ai/changelog/2026-10-02-remove-description-attachments-without-duplicates-htpr-6629/",
      "title": "Remove description attachments without duplicates",
      "content_text": "When you edited a task description containing file attachments, closing the editor could lead to unexpected behavior. Previously, a bug caused incorrect file handling during attachment removal, where removing one file would result in the other files being duplicated in storage.\n\nThe fix ([HTPR-6629](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-339/6629)) ensures that when you open a task, edit the description, remove an attachment you don't want, and save, only the items you deselected are removed. Remaining attachments are preserved as exactly one copy each.\n\n**What you can do now**\n\n- Attach multiple files to a task description (e.g., for a design review or documentation).\n- Open the description, click the attachment you want to remove, and save.\n- All other attachments persist exactly once, without duplicates.\n\nThe change mainly affects the Task Reporter workflow: anyone you've added as a Task Reporter on a task can edit the description and remove attachments without artifacts.\n\n## Related tickets\n\n- [https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/6629](https://app.hypertask.ai/detail/project-15/6629)",
      "summary": "Fixed a bug where removing a file from a task description would incorrectly save a duplicate of the remaining file. When you had multiple attachments and removed one, only one copy of each remaining file now persists.",

        "Tasks"
      ],
